land.text: the Kangra hill country, which Sansar Chand 'surrendered' to Maharaja Ranjit Singh by the treaty of Jawalamukhi in 1809

successors.note: Infobox 'Annexation by the Sikh Empire: 1810', 'Succeeded by: Sikh Empire'; the body text dates the treaty 1809. The Sikh dossier's gain uses the same region. Kangra-Lambagraon survived as a 20-village princely estate of 324 km2 and acceded to India in 1947; it is not drawn.

capitals.name: Kangra fort (Nagarkot, Kot Kangra)
capitals.note: A reading: the Kangra State page names no capital, only 'the fortress of Kangra' (Kangra State page: the fort 'surrendered in November, 1620'). The Katoch page: 'The Kangra fort was known as Nagarkot or Kot Kangra'. The Nurpur State page has the Trigarta kingdom 'shifted its capital from Doab Jalandhar to Kangra Fort in 1070 A.D.', so 1050-1069 is the same reading. No capital is drawn for 1621-1788: the Mughals held the fort and no page opened names the Katoch rajas' seat (the Sujanpur Tira pages did not load).

capitals.name: Kangra fort (Nagarkot, Kot Kangra)
capitals.note: Sansar Chand 'succeeded in recovering the ancient fort of his ancestors, in 1789' (Kangra State page); same reading as above. The Sansar Chand page names Nadaun only as one of his forts and the place 'where Maharaja Sansar Chand spent his last days', not as a capital.

correction.text: the Kangra hill country round the fortress of Kangra, cut to Himachal Pradesh and without the seats of Chamba and Nurpur

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page gives no area and no boundary, only 'Established: 11th century' [citation needed]. Drawn as the 60 km disc round the fort (the radius the Sikh dossier uses for its 1809 gain), intersected with Himachal Pradesh, minus a 30 km disc round Chamba town (32.56 N 76.13 E) and a 20 km disc round Nurpur town (32.30 N 75.88 E): 27 cells (about 6,830 km2) of the disc's 39. Review 2026-11-01: the first draft took in the seats of Chamba and Nurpur and 5 cells of the Punjab plain; this dossier's own 1794 event has Chamba and Nurpur as separate states fighting Sansar Chand, and the Chamba State page has Chamba town as that state's capital 'Chamba (920-1948)'. Guler, which split from Kangra in 1405 ('founded in 1405 by Raja Hari Chand, a scion of the ancient royal family of Kangra', Guler State page), is not separated: no page opened gives a boundary between Guler and Kangra. No infobox area to compare. The Sikh dossier's 1809 gain still uses the full 60 km disc.

minus.text: the fort of Kangra and the surrounding area that Jahangir annexed in 1620

correction.text: the Kangra hill country (as 1050-1619) without the fort and its surrounding area, which the Mughals took in 1620; the Katoch rajas stayed on as vassals

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Jahangir successfully subdued the fort in 1620 annexing the surrounding area and reducing the Katoch rajas to the status of vassals.' The page gives no radius for the surrounding area; 25 km (7 cells, all inside the 27-cell shape) is the reading. Ends in 1782: the Mughal hold ended in 1783 (next keyframe). The Katoch page: 'Then they were brought under the Mughal suzerainty by the emperor Jehangir'; the Kangra Fort page has Dharam Chand submitting to Akbar in 1556 and agreeing to pay tribute. The Mughal dossier carries no Kangra event and no vassal_start for the Katoch rajas (a gap for its owner; the vassal_start belongs in the suzerain's ledger).

minus.text: the fort of Kangra itself, held by the Kanhaiya misl until Sansar Chand recovered it

correction.text: the Kangra hill country with the surrounding area back in Katoch hands but the fort still outside

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Sansar Chand rallied an army, ousted the then ruler of Kangra, Saif Ali Khan, and gained possession of his patrimony. This happened in 1783, and Sansar Chand was aided by the Kanhaiya misl'; the fort itself is recovered only 'in 1789' (same page). The Kangra Fort page has the fort 'surrendered in 1783 by his son to the Sikh leader, Jai Singh Kanhaiya', so the fort cell stays out; the 5 km disc (1 cell) is the reading for the fort. Neither page gives the extent of the land that returned in 1783.

correction.text: the Kangra hill country with its ancient fort recovered, cut to Himachal Pradesh and without the seats of Chamba and Nurpur

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Sansar Chand 'reigned over a relatively large part of present-day Himachal Pradesh for some two decades' by overrunning 'other nearby principalities' (Kangra State page: 'compelled the submission of their rulers'); no page gives their names, dates or extent, so the shape stays the 27-cell core, a minimum (the Kangra Fort page adds only 'In 1805 he turned his attention to Bilaspur'). After 1806 the Sansar Chand page says he was 'left with no territory beyond the immediate vicinity of the fortress of Kangra'; the Kangra Fort page has the fort besieged in 1807 and 'most of the land of Kangra jagir' incorporated into Nepal by early 1809. The Nepal dossier draws 1806-1809 as a contest, so this shape is kept to 1809. Same cut as the first keyframe (Chamba and Nurpur seats removed after review 2026-11-01).

region.text: the Kangra hill country round the fortress of Kangra

ledger.note: 11th century (bridging year 1050): the Katoch state of Kangra. Infobox 'Established: 11th century', tagged [citation needed]; the page is silent on the founding year, the founder and the capital. The Katoch page (read 2026-11-01) gives no date either: 'The tradition holds that the Katoch were the rulers of Kangra from the times of Mahabharata'; 'The originator of the clan was Rajanaka Bhumi Chand'. The Nurpur State page has the Trigarta kingdom shifting 'its capital from Doab Jalandhar to Kangra Fort in 1070 A.D.', which fits the 11th century. The year is the middle of the century; confidence stays 1.

region.text: the fort of Kangra and 'the surrounding area'

ledger.note: November 1620: Jahangir takes Kangra fort. 'Jahangir successfully subdued the fort in 1620 annexing the surrounding area and reducing the Katoch rajas to the status of vassals'; 'After a siege of 14 months, the fort surrendered in November, 1620.' The rest of the hill country stays with the Katoch rajas as Mughal vassals; the Mughal dossier carries no matching gain or vassal_start.

region.text: the land round Kangra fort (the 'patrimony'), without the fort itself

ledger.note: 1783: the Mughal hold on Kangra ends. 'Sansar Chand rallied an army, ousted the then ruler of Kangra, Saif Ali Khan, and gained possession of his patrimony. This happened in 1783, and Sansar Chand was aided by the Kanhaiya misl.' The Sansar Chand page calls Saifu Ali Khan Kaymkhani 'the Mughal governor of Kangra' and gives no year. The Kangra Fort page says the fort was 'surrendered in 1783 by his son to the Sikh leader, Jai Singh Kanhaiya', so only the land round the fort (25 km minus the 5 km fort disc, a reading of 'patrimony') is drawn as returning; the fort follows in 1789. Year the page's; region my reading. The Mughal dossier carries no matching loss.

region.text: the ancient fort of Kangra (one cell)

ledger.note: 1789: Sansar Chand recovers Kangra fort. 'Raja Sansar Chand II succeeded in recovering the ancient fort of his ancestors, in 1789.' The page does not say who held the fort from 1783 to 1789. The Kangra Fort page says it was surrendered in 1783 'to the Sikh leader, Jai Singh Kanhaiya' (Kanhaiya misl) and that 'In 1786, Raja Sansar Chand gained Kangra fort by peaceful treaty with Jai Singh Kanhaiya' in return for territorial concessions in the Punjab; that page does not mention 1789. 1789 is kept (Kangra State page); the counterpart is sikh-confederacy (the Kanhaiya misl; the Sikh Confederacy dossier ends 1799 and has no Kangra event, and no Kanhaiya misl dossier exists). The Sansar Chand page says only that he 'ousted the Mughal governor of Kangra, Saifu Ali Khan Kaymkhani'. Confidence 2: the year is disputed between the two pages and the holder is the Fort page's.

region.text: the Rohlu (Rehlu) territory, inside the state's own core

ledger.note: 1794: Sansar Chand wins at Rehlu. 'In the historic Battle of Rehlu (1794)' Chamba and the Raja of Nurpur fought him (the chief of Guler on his side); 'Chamba's Raja Raj Singh was killed, and the Rohlu territory passed into the hands of the Katoch chief'. The Sansar Chand page places the battle 'in the Rehlu region, near present-day Rait village'; the Rait page (17.5 km from Dharamshala, 7.5 km from Gaggal airport) gives no coordinates, says Raj Singh 'died on the battlefield at Nerti' and has Sansar Chand trying 'to seize the Rihlu territory'. The gazetteer lacks Rait and no page gives coordinates, so the region is the state's own core (it moves no cells); Chamba has no dossier. Confidence 1: the page does not delimit the land.

region.text: the country round Kangra fort, where the Gorkha army besieged Sansar Chand

ledger.note: 1806: the Gorkhas invade Kangra. 'The Gorkhas and the recently humbled hill-states allied to invade Kangra in 1806'; 'Sansar Chand was defeated and left with no territory beyond the immediate vicinity of the fortress of Kangra'. Same zone as the Nepal dossier (Cliopatria's 1807 salient). The page also says the Gorkhas 'could not capture Kangra Fort'; the Amar Singh Thapa page says they 'ultimately captured the fort'. The Kangra Fort page dates the siege of the fort to 1807 ('In 1807, Kangra Fort ... was put under siege') and says that 'By early 1809, most of the land of Kangra jagir had been incorporated into Nepal, although the fort still held out'.

1809: Sansar Chand gives Kangra to Ranjit Singh. 'In this despair, the Sansar Chand treated with Ranjit Singh at Jawalamukhi in 1809'; 'Raja Sansar Chand surrendered his (now largely notional) state to Maharaja Ranjit Singh.' The infobox dates the Sikh annexation 1810; the Sansar Chand page says the fort 'came under Maharaja Ranjit Singh in 1809'.

region.text: the Kangra hill country, passing to the Sikh Empire

ledger.note: 1809: the state of Kangra ends in the Sikh Empire. 'Raja Sansar Chand surrendered his (now largely notional) state to Maharaja Ranjit Singh'; infobox 'Succeeded by: Sikh Empire' (annexation 1810).

region.text: the Kangra country, given up by the Gorkhas

ledger.note: 24 August 1809: the Gorkhas return to the Sutlej. 'Bada Amar returned to Sutlej river as per agreement on 24 August 1809 AD.' The page gives no terms; the Kangra State page has Sansar Chand treating 'with Ranjit Singh at Jawalamukhi in 1809'.

wars.name: Mughal siege of Kangra Fort (1619-1620)

zones.text: the fort of Kangra and its surrounding area

wars.outcome: The fort surrenders to Jahangir in November 1620 after a siege of 14 months; the surrounding area is annexed and the Katoch rajas become vassals.
wars.note: Start year 1619 is arithmetic (14 months before November 1620); the page also says the fort 'resisted Mughal Emperor Akbar's siege' without a year.

wars.name: Battle of Rehlu
wars.outcome: Sansar Chand wins; Raja Raj Singh of Chamba is killed and the Rohlu territory passes to the Katoch chief.
wars.note: The page names Chamba and the Raja of Nurpur against Sansar Chand, 'supported by the chief of Guler'. No zone is given because the page does not place Rohlu.

wars.name: Gorkha invasion of Kangra
wars.outcome: The Gorkhas defeat Sansar Chand in 1806 but do not take the fort (Sansar Chand page); Sansar Chand turns to Ranjit Singh and Amar Singh Thapa's army returns to the Sutlej on 24 August 1809.
wars.note: The Amar Singh Thapa page says the Gorkhas 'ultimately captured the fort' and also has Sansar Chand 'aided by 1500 soldiers of Sikh Maharaja Ranjit Singh' fighting at Ganesh Valley; it gives no start for the siege.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a frontier of the state in any year; the shapes are radii round the fortress of Kangra, cut to Himachal Pradesh and without the discs round Chamba and Nurpur.

sources.title: Kangra State

sources.title: Sansar Chand

sources.title: Amar Singh Thapa

sources.title: Kangra Fort
sources.note: Mughal hold 1620-1783, fort surrendered in 1783 to Jai Singh Kanhaiya, 1786 treaty, 1805-1809; names no Katoch capital and does not mention 1789.

sources.title: Katoch
sources.note: No founding date (Mahabharata tradition, Rajanaka Bhumi Chand); fort called Nagarkot or Kot Kangra; Mughal suzerainty under Jehangir.

sources.title: Rait, Himachal Pradesh
sources.note: Rait 17.5 km from Dharamshala; Raj Singh of Chamba died at Nerti in 1794; no coordinates.

sources.title: Guler State
sources.note: Founded 1405 by Raja Hari Chand, a scion of the Kangra royal family; capital Haripur Guler; annexed by the Sikh Empire in 1813.

sources.title: Chamba State
sources.note: Capitals Bharmour (580-920) and Chamba (920-1948); Raj Singh 1764-1794 in the ruler table; accession 1948.

sources.title: Nurpur State

notes: No Cliopatria row. The pages give the state no boundary and no capital (Kangra State page: capital, area, dissolution date and predecessor all silent), so every shape is a reading: the 60 km disc round the fort at 76.27 E, 32.1 N (the point and radius the Sikh dossier uses), intersected with Himachal Pradesh and minus 30 km round Chamba town and 20 km round Nurpur town (27 cells), after the review of 2026-11-01 found that the plain disc took in the seats of those two states. Guler (founded 1405 from the Kangra royal family, Guler State page; capital Haripur Guler; annexed by the Sikhs 1813) is not separated. Capital: Kangra fort (a reading; no page names a capital), none drawn 1621-1788. The founding year is a bridge for 'the 11th century' [citation needed]; the Katoch page gives no date. Mughal exit and recovery: the Kangra State page has Sansar Chand oust the Mughal governor Saif Ali Khan in 1783 with the Kanhaiya misl and recover the fort in 1789; the Kangra Fort page has the fort surrendered in 1783 to Jai Singh Kanhaiya and gained by Sansar Chand by treaty in 1786 and does not mention 1789. The dossier draws the land round the fort back in 1783 (Mughal counterpart) and the fort in 1789 (sikh-confederacy, the Kanhaiya misl). Sansar Chand's expansion over neighbouring hill states (Kangra State page: 'overran other nearby principalities and compelled the submission of their rulers'; Sansar Chand page: 'a relatively large part of present-day Himachal Pradesh') is undated and unnamed, so no gain is drawn; a gap-filler should open Kullu, Mandi, Kahlur and Bilaspur pages. Reign dates: the Sansar Chand page's infobox gives 1758-1824 while its text says c. 1765-1824, the Katoch page 1775-1823; no ruler strip. Mughal dossier gaps: no vassal_start for the Katoch rajas from 1620 (to 1783), no loss for 1783 and no Kangra event at all. Chamba (Chamba State page: Bharmour 580-920, Chamba 920-1948), Nurpur (Nurpur State page: founded 1064, annexed 1815 by the Sikhs, 1849 by the British) and Guler have no dossiers. Wikidata id left null. The Sikh Empire dossier's 1809 gain still uses the plain 60 km disc, which includes the Chamba and Nurpur seats; the Nepal contest events agree with the years here.
